reading.body:
Amazon Web Services recorded $717 billion in revenue in 2025 while operating two major AI product lines: SageMaker for full-stack ML lifecycle management and Bedrock for managed foundation model access.

AWS sits at the intersection of compute supply and AI demand. SageMaker's architecture—unified data lakes, model monitoring, bias detection, and governance tools—reflects the infrastructure required to run production AI at scale. Bedrock's API model with VPC support and IAM integration suggests AWS is positioning itself as the managed layer between foundation models and enterprise users who want isolation and control. Both products point to a company treating AI not as a feature but as a platform business spanning data, compute, and model serving.

The scale here matters for power and buildings. A $717 billion revenue company in cloud services operates data centers globally to deliver these products. The fact that SageMaker includes toxicity detection, guardrails, and data lineage tracking indicates AWS is building compliance and observability into the compute layer itself. This is not decorative. As regulatory exposure grows, the infrastructure provider that bakes governance into the platform gains advantage over those that bolt it on later.

The data does not specify AWS's capital spending, energy consumption, or data center locations. It does not break out AI revenue from total AWS revenue or show whether SageMaker and Bedrock are growing faster than legacy services. It does not name which foundation models Bedrock serves or how much compute AWS allocates to these two products versus others.

profile_text.body:
Amazon Web Services is a subsidiary of Amazon providing cloud computing services. According to its website, Amazon SageMaker functions as "the center for all your data, analytics, and AI," offering an integrated development environment that unifies data access, analytics, and machine learning capabilities. The company describes SageMaker Unified Studio as bringing together ML and analytics tools in a single workspace, with features including distributed training, model deployment, generative AI application development, and SQL analytics accelerated by Amazon Q Developer.

SageMaker covers the full AI lifecycle with tools for model training, customization, and deployment on performant infrastructure, along with capabilities for inference, governance, and observability. The platform emphasizes enterprise security through built-in governance, fine-grained access controls via Amazon SageMaker Catalog, data classification, toxicity detection, guardrails, and responsible AI policies. It integrates with Amazon S3 data lakes and Amazon Redshift data warehouses using a lakehouse architecture with Apache Iceberg compatibility and federated query support across third-party data sources. AWS also operates AWS Bedrock, a managed foundation model API service that includes IAM integration, VPC support, model evaluation tools, and AgentCore for agent orchestration.

Amazon Web Services is a public company headquartered in Seattle, Washington, with 2024 revenue of $716,924,000,000 according to its 10-K filing. The company is tracked in connection with a lawsuit, Haugland v. Anthropic PBC, in the District Court of Delaware.
